original.target_description: Study 1: combined looking, approaching and contact person-oriented point-sample scores across crying, humming and talking; within-dog repeated-measures ANOVA main effect of condition.

n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this behavioral analysis; 18 dogs participated and the reported repeated-measures degrees of freedom are consistent with the full sample.
n.location: Article p. 3, Method—Participants; p. 6, Results (PDF pp. 4 and 7 including cover)
n.quote: Eighteen medium-sized domestic dogs (Canis familiaris) from the North West USA participated in the study.

es.location: Article p. 6, Results, paragraph describing Figure 2 (PDF p. 7 including cover)

p.location: Article p. 6, Results, same repeated-measures ANOVA (PDF p. 7 including cover)

replication.target_description: Study 1: repeated-measures ANOVA main effect of emotion (crying, laughing, baseline talking) on summed person-oriented behaviours (looking, contacting, approaching, vocalizing), across owner/stranger conditions in domestic dogs tested at home. Located on article p. 238 (PDF p. 4).

n.sample_role: Dogs with complete behavioural coding for the repeated-measures behavioural analysis.
n.exclusions: 16 dog-owner pairs tested; one dog had behavioural data only for owner crying because of a camera malfunction. Heart-rate exclusions are separate from this behavioural test.
n.location: p. 238 (PDF p. 4), Data Analysis; total recruited sample p. 237, Participants
n.quote: Another dog only had behavioural data for the owner crying … condition because of a camera malfunction. This left behavioural … data for 14 dogs who had data in all heart rate conditions and 15 dogs … with full data in behavioural coding.

es.location: p. 238 (PDF p. 4), Results, Behavioural Data, first paragraph; partial metric identified in Data Analysis on same page

p.location: p. 238 (PDF p. 4), Results, Behavioural Data, first paragraph (emotion main effect)

reported_success.quote: In this experiment, we replicated the Custance and Mayer … (2012) study as expected.

notes:
Original target is the omnibus condition main effect, rather than a post-hoc comparison or the crying-person versus silent-witness test. Original PDF includes an extra ResearchGate cover; article p. 6 is PDF p. 7. The text extraction renders the printed less-than glyph as a backslash; statistical quotes normalize that glyph. Full replication paper unavailable: DOI landing and PsycNet PDF returned 403; Unpaywall and OpenAlex reported no open copy; Europe PMC reported no full text; primary OSF project zadty contains only a .sav data file and has no child projects; preprint/open-access searches found no full manuscript. ResearchGate exposes only first-page publisher preview; this was not treated as the full paper or used for statistical extraction. Replication statistics and authors narrative verdict left unverified.
Source follow-up: Published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service; supplied text title, authors and DOI match the assigned replication reference. Replication replaces humming with laughing. Effect size retained as printed; Data Analysis explicitly identifies effect-size measures as partial eta-squared. Printed F degrees of freedom (2, 15) retained without correction; the methods explicitly state 15 dogs with full behavioural coding, while other behavioural tests use denominator df 14 or 28. No sample size inferred from those degrees of freedom. Text extraction uses font glyphs ⫽, ⬍ and ␩2 in quoted statistics. Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not a finding that its source is unavailable.
